Question: Point \(D\) is on side \(CB\) of triangle \(ABC.\) If \(\angle CAD=\angle DAB=60^\circ,\) \(AC=3\) and \(AB=6,\) then the length of \(AD\) is
Solution:
The two \(60^\circ\) angles give \(\angle CAB=120^\circ\). Extending one side at \(A\) therefore creates a \(60^\circ\) angle, which lets us construct an equilateral triangle.

Extend \(BA\) beyond \(A\) to a point \(E\) with \(AE=AC=3\). Since \(AE\) and \(AB\) are opposite rays,
\[
\angle CAE=180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ.
\]
The isosceles triangle \(ACE\) has a \(60^\circ\) vertex angle, so all its angles are \(60^\circ\). Thus it is equilateral and \(CE=3\). Also, \(\angle ACE=\angle CAD=60^\circ\), so the equal alternate interior angles give \(CE\parallel AD\).

Now \(A\) lies on \(BE\), \(D\) lies on \(BC\), and \(AD\parallel EC\). Therefore \(\triangle BAD\) and \(\triangle BEC\) are similar by equal angles. Corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{AD}{EC}=\frac{BA}{BE}
=\frac{6}{6+3}=\frac23.
\]
Consequently, \(AD=3\cdot\frac23=2\), choice A.
